## Description

> AI-agent disclosure: this PR was authored by an automated agent (Codex
/ GPT-6) and has not been line-by-line reviewed by a human before
submission.

The Codespaces setup still selects Node 18 through an assumed `nvs.sh`
installation and forces ESLint/Prettier presets after the repository
moved to Oxc. Refresh the setup while continuing to use the default
Codespaces image, including its Node runtime, GitHub CLI, and other
developer tools.

- Read the NVS release tag and commit pin directly from the legacy
bundle commands in `.github/workflows/build-status.yml`, failing if
either is missing, malformed, or duplicated. This keeps CI as the single
source of truth. Initialize NVS in Bash and Zsh, and expose its
executable to legacy tests without selecting an older Node version.
- Install the pnpm version from `devEngines.packageManager.version`
using [pnpm's documented standalone Docker
installer](https://pnpm.io/installation#in-a-docker-container). Put its
bin directory first on PATH, preserve `--frozen-lockfile
--ignore-scripts` for workspace dependencies, and wait for setup before
connecting.
- Replace stale editor extensions with Oxc and GitHub Actions, disable
inherited ESLint, and keep the Oxc default formatter, format-on-save,
and sticky scroll together in the dev container presets. Remove
`.vscode/settings.json` so these preferences apply to Codespaces.
- Consolidate lifecycle setup into a fail-fast script, document
Codespaces usage, and add an empty changeset (no published package
impact).

The configuration intentionally omits an image definition: [Codespaces
supports falling back to its default
image](https://docs.github.com/en/codespaces/setting-up-your-project-for-codespaces/adding-a-dev-container-configuration/introduction-to-dev-containers#using-the-default-dev-container-configuration).
GitHub CLI is already included, so no additional feature or installation
is needed.

### Validation

- Passed JSON parsing, official common devcontainer-property and VS Code
extension-list schema checks, shell syntax, and `git diff --check`. The
generic full schema's image requirement does not model the Codespaces
fallback.
- Exercised fresh/repeated setup with real Node and stubbed
network/install commands: pinned NVS revision, Bash/Zsh profile
selection, pnpm version and installer environment, PATH precedence over
preinstalled pnpm, dependency flags, temporary-file cleanup, changing
both NVS pins in CI without changing the setup script, rejection of
missing/malformed/duplicate CI pins, and failure propagation for NVS
validation/installation, download, pnpm bootstrap, and dependency
installation.
- Exercised upstream NVS v1.7.1 profile installation with surrounding
dependencies mocked: existing profile content preserved, repeated setup
idempotent, and sourcing its actual Bash initialization defines `nvs`
without changing the default Node path. NVS is invoked in a child
process because its shell initialization is incompatible with `set -u`.
- A live Codespaces rebuild, real tool downloads, dependency
installation, and repository format/test commands remain untested in
this environment. Before marking ready, rebuild a codespace and check
`gh --version`, `nvs --version`, `pnpm --version`, `pnpm --filter
fast-check build`, and `pnpm format:check`; also try `nvs add 22` and
`nvs use 22` in a terminal.
